{{Short description|Relation between conic sections and triangles}}
{{Other|Carnot's theorem (disambiguation)}}
[[File:Carnot conic.svg|thumb|upright=1.0|6 points on the sides of triangle and their common conic section]]
'''Carnot's theorem''', named after [[Lazare Carnot]] ({{IPAc-en|lang|k|ɑːr|ˈ|n|oʊ}} {{respell|kar|NOH}}, {{IPA|fr|kaʁno|lang}}), describes a relation between [[conic section]]s and [[triangle]]s.

In a triangle <math>ABC</math> with points <math>C_A, C_B</math> on the side <math>AB</math>, <math>A_B, A_C</math> on the side <math>BC</math> and <math>B_C, B_A</math> on the side <math>AC</math> those six points are located on a common conic section if and only if the following equation holds:

:<math>
\frac{|AC_A|}{|BC_A|}\cdot \frac{|AC_B|}{|BC_B|}\cdot \frac{|BA_B|}{|CA_B|}\cdot \frac{|BA_C|}{|CA_C|} \cdot \frac{|CB_C|}{|AB_C|}\cdot \frac{|CB_A|}{|AB_A|}=1
</math>.
